pr_title: Handle postgresql database not found error more gracefully
pr_body:
### Summary

Fixes #41606 

```ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PostgreSQLAdapter.new_client``` method had this logic to handle errors such way that if error message had ```dbName``` then raise exception  ```ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError```

But there can be scenarios when ```dbName``` and ```host``` values  are same and ```host``` value is invalid.

So in that scenario actual error from ```PG.connect``` method is related to unable to establish connection.

But error returned was  ```ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError```


I have made changes to return ```ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError``` in more explicit scenario.
pr_comments: The checks which are failing are not related to changes introduced in this PR
This sounds like it would only work if the server generates the error message in an `en` locale -- which I assume is why the existing implementation only looks for a mention of the database name.

This error is returned by `PG` gem, couldn't find any internationalization happening there.

Is internationalization taken care by rails for these errors @matthewd ?

@matthewd Since you were already looking at it. The change looks good to me and I kinda like that it passes the entire error message that was returned from the database server back to the user. cc @kamipo

issue_context.title: ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PostgreSQLAdapter.new_client raises NoDatabaseError erroneously
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
Have a database.yml that includes a database name, and the hostname also includes the database name. The hostname should not be resolveable. Try to connect. 

### Expected behavior
A ActiveRecord::ConnectionNotEstablished error is raised.

### Actual behavior
A ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError is raised:
`could not translate host name "clusterX" to address: Name or service not known`

The problem is you're just checking the exception message for the database name, instead of _also_ checking if it is actually a "database does not exist" error. 

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.1.3
**Ruby version**: 2.7.2

The problem is how PostgreSQLAdapter  `new_client` method is rescuing the error.

>           else
